agent_priors_used: Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: a research program that has run 395 experiments and produced no VALIDATED claim usually does not have a hypothesis problem; it has a subject-validity problem. When the arm under test is structurally incapable of executing, every comparison is uninformative regardless of how carefully it is designed. I therefore rank 'make the treatment capable of happening' above 'design a better comparison' whenever the treatment is absent. The specific fact that SPIDER's inherited arm is absent is repository evidence I verified directly, not this prior.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: a comparison is uninformative unless the baseline is strong and the instrument has dynamic range. Strong baselines are usually reconstructions of the competitor's mechanism rather than the competitor's own artifact, because headline artifacts depend on infrastructure that is usually absent - which is why the missing arm in this program is a key-free reconstruction of the published competitors, not an attempt to run their code.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: an experiment that is structurally barred by its own preregistration from producing the outcome its mission is chartered to produce is a bad use of a scarce lane, however elegantly it is designed. This is the general form of the argument that moved me off Frontier's inherited handoff; the specific bar is quoted from the frozen mandate text, which is SPIDER evidence.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: in long-horizon tool-using systems, the dominant failure is compounding path dependence and silent capability loss through merge and branch divergence rather than shortage of ideas. I use it to insist that a recovered capability be pinned by hash and re-verified after merge, not merely restored once.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: when a site's own interface already exposes a sufficient abstraction, cross-episode learned inheritance can be strictly dominated by a no-memory executor that calls site primitives. I treat this as a serious architectural competitor that SPIDER has never tested, which is why I made it Frontier's objective; I do not treat the published WALT-family numbers as SPIDER evidence for it.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: in agent memory research, a registry that constrains exploration can be net-negative on novel tasks because of the exploration/exploitation asymmetry. A program that only measures inherited-mechanism benefit will systematically overestimate it. This is why I regard inherited-mechanism harm as the largest unasked question, and why I accept deferring it one cycle rather than pretending it is answered.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: a reusable validated control is worth more than a fresh hypothesis when many independent experiments have failed on control quality, because it converts a per-packet reminder that has failed eight times into a substrate artifact. This is the general prior behind Runtime's control-contract export, which is the one genuinely new element I am adding to a live thread.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: for local-attractor flags, the correct test is not experiment count but decision value - whether any possible outcome of the next experiment can change a decision that is currently open. This is the criterion I applied to reject Frontier's handoff despite its being well designed, and it is the same criterion under which I let Physics continue.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Against continuing the inherited handoff, which targets a 618-line kernel at commit 15306b5b that exists in no working tree: its economic threshold of 0.85 was already rejected as non-identifying by a previous Director, and executing it would reproduce a MEASUREMENT_INVALID. Two of its contents are correct and I fold them in rather than discard them - re-measure the cold baseline with genuinely executed multi-step discovery, and preserve the URL prefix in any action template - so superseding the handoff does not mean discarding its content. Against C-PARAM-INHERIT as the target claim: the mechanism half is already adjudicated EXPERIMENTAL by EXP-PRODUCT-36249064252 with 150/150 never-observed-resource-B transfers at binding accuracy 1.0; only the economic half is unidentified, and re-running the mechanism half would re-litigate a settled question instead of answering the open one. Against C-LLM-INHERIT, which is this lane's most product-central claim: OPENAI_API_KEY is absent on this runner and BrowserGym requires a GHCR pull behind a non-interactive docker login that has already failed, so no design of that experiment is executable this cycle - it is unmeasurable, not unfinished, and it stays the first reactivation once a key and a browser exist. Against parking Product until Runtime delivers a substrate: the kernel recovery and the head-to-head design are Product's to own, neither needs a browser or a key, and Runtime can deliver its authenticated control matrix in parallel, so parking would idle the critical path for no reason. I did not flag Product for cognitive reset and did not perform one; the direction is right and the only defect was a dangling dependency, which I am fixing.

allocation.question: With the accepted parameterized-inheritance capability recovered durably and pinned by exact hash (commit 664bc124, src/spider/kernel.py sha256 ac1cbdd9..., tests/test_kernel.py sha256 efcd6649...) and re-verified as executable in Product's own branch after merge rather than only in a working tree, does inherited mechanism execution beat the strongest available alternatives on amortized end-to-end cost at matched correctness, on a substrate whose cold-exploration arm has real preregistered dynamic range and whose baselines are honestly executed rather than policy-fixed? The mandatory comparison set is: inherited parameterized mechanisms; the no-memory deterministic executor compiled from the current observation alone; a cold discovery baseline that actually performs multi-step auth, pagination traversal and schema discovery per task; literal replay; and retrieval-k5. Two self-containment requirements are binding this cycle. FIRST, the no-memory deterministic executor must be built in-lane if the pinned reference arm this cycle's portfolio expected from Intel is not present at freeze; a missing baseline is a fail-loud stop, never a silent substitution with a weaker arm. SECOND, as a hard pre-arm gate that runs and is logged before any candidate arm: the cold arm must cost strictly more than the treatment on the positive-control task set by a preregistered margin, otherwise the packet reports the dynamic-range deficit as its finding rather than an economic ratio - the exact defect that made EXP-PRODUCT-36249064252 and EXP-PRODUCT-36272385776 both non-identifying. The two product defects already on the record must be resolved rather than re-measured: literal distill() confidence 0.5 against min_confidence 0.8, and URL-prefix loss in any action-template builder. A falsifier must be pre-declared in the direction that would force the architecture to change.
allocation.rationale: This is the most decision-relevant experiment available in the program, and it is in flight and pre-freeze with a sound design. I verified independently that the two substrate defects it must fix are real in the canonical tree: the shipped distill() hardcodes confidence 0.5 against a default min_confidence of 0.8, which is precisely the arithmetic behind Frontier's measured 0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions, and the action-template path-prefix loss is the audit-confirmed critical finding in EXP-PRODUCT-36272385776 that produced its 0.0 positive control. So the treatment arm is absent for a reason that is cheap, local, and provable, and this is the only lane authorized to own src/. I am making one correction rather than changing the direction. The previous mandate lists Intel's pinned no-memory deterministic executor as a parallel dependency, but Intel was never allocated an experiment in that batch and is idle with active_experiment_id null, so the mandatory comparison set contained an arm that no one was building - the precise condition that sank the last two economic packets, where baselines were policy-fixed or absent and the ratio therefore meant nothing. I am requiring the arm to be built in-lane with a fail-loud stop if it is missing, so that this packet cannot repeat that failure mode. Everything else in the design stands: recover by pinned hash, re-verify after merge, execute cold discovery for real, and gate on dynamic range before reading any arm.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: The previous cycle (36278764892) reached the right diagnosis and I confirm it from the repository, but the portfolio has since lost two lanes to hard execution failures and has never started its fifth. Four findings drive this cycle. (1) THE INHERITED ARM DOES NOT EXIST IN THE CANONICAL TREE, AND I VERIFIED IT MYSELF. src/spider/kernel.py at main HEAD is 132 lines. It contains no distill_parameterized, no parameter induction, and no semantic resolution of any kind: resolve() admits a mechanism only when m.intent == intent, an exact string equality, so 'goals resolved to applicable mechanisms without internal ids' is structurally impossible rather than merely unproven. Its only distiller, distill(), hardcodes confidence=0.5 while resolve() requires confidence >= min_confidence (default 0.8), so no mechanism the shipped kernel can produce can ever reach EXECUTABLE. Frontier's independent audit of EXP-FRONTIER-36249071934 measured the same fact from the other side: 0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions, 0 mechanisms executed, C_i == C_c exactly, and required_fix #1 is that the inherited arm 'must be made executable before any architecture verdict on C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY is possible'. So across 395 canonical experiments there are zero VALIDATED and zero PRODUCT_CORE claims, and every 'inherited execution versus alternative' comparison run to date had a structurally non-executing incumbent as one of its two arms. This is not a scientific negative; it is an absent subject. (2) THE PROXIMATE CAUSE OF THIS CYCLE'S FAILURES IS NON-DISCRIMINATING INSTRUMENTS, NOT BAD HYPOTHESES. The two independent packets that produced real outcomes both failed for this reason: in EXP-PRODUCT-36272385776 the positive control PC-SAME-RESOURCE returned success_rate 0.0 against a preregistered >=0.95 and the null control NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT fired anyway (6 mechanisms induced), and the audit traced both to a single construction bug rather than to induction failing; in EXP-PRODUCT-36249064252 the inherited arm was executable and beat every baseline, yet the economic gate had zero dynamic range because cold exploration already cost 1.0 HTTP request per task on that substrate. The registered C-MEAS-VALID next_gate already says the right thing in the right words - 'writable/auth/session/drift controls must produce DISCriminating positive and null outcomes' - and eight claims are MEASUREMENT_INVALID because that word was treated as an aspiration rather than as a precondition. (3) THE ENVIRONMENT REMOVES THREE CLAIMS FROM THIS CYCLE'S REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT, NOT A BACKLOG. I checked this runner directly: playwright is not importable, /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright does not exist, and no OPENAI_API_KEY is present. BrowserGym additionally requires a GHCR pull behind a docker login that has already failed non-interactively. C-LLM-INHERIT and every browser-capture variant of C-WEB-DYNAMICS, C-MEAS-VALID and C-PRODUCT-ECON are therefore unmeasurable here regardless of design quality, and the frozen Runtime preflight names a chromium-1243 path that does not exist on this machine. Allocating lanes to those paths a third time is not persistence. (4) INTEL IS IDLE AND IS A NAMED DEPENDENCY OF WORK THAT IS ALREADY RUNNING. Product's pre-freeze EXP-PRODUCT-36279245734 lists 'Intel's pinned runnable no-memory deterministic executor reference arm (this cycle, parallel)' among its mandatory comparison arms, and Frontier's frozen mandate says the verified external regime boundaries should set Frontier's novelty-rate sweep. No Intel experiment was ever allocated in that batch (active_experiment_id is null, active_stage IDLE), so three lanes are pointed at an owner that does not exist. That is the clearest liveness failure in the program and the cheapest high-leverage thing I can repair. Consequently this cycle does not generate new claims. Four lanes execute or repair transactions that are already aimed at the identification problem, and the two lanes with no live transaction (Frontier, whose experiment died in execute with a non-retryable exit 66, and Intel, which never started) get objectives chosen to attack the same decision from outside their local basins. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are deferred at portfolio level for a stated reason rather than by omission: both already hold valid synthetic single-resource SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST results, both next_gates require session/auth/drift/perturbation substrates that do not exist here, and both are the first claims to reactivate the moment Runtime's authenticated control matrix lands. The single largest question left unasked this cycle, stated plainly rather than hidden: SPIDER has never tested whether inherited mechanisms cause HARM - a stale or mis-bound mechanism forcing a confidently wrong action - only whether they help. I am accepting that cost deliberately, because the question presupposes an executable inherited arm and Product's pre-freeze recovery is its precondition; it is the first question the next cycle should ask.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout brief was materially useful and I adopted its central diagnosis, but I corrected its role assignments and rejected one of its proposals outright. ADOPTED: that the inherited-versus-no-memory leg is unidentified and the incumbent kernel is non-executable; that browser provisioning is a hard block rather than an engineering backlog; that Frontier's 9-experiment concentration on C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY is a local attractor warranting a cognitive reset; that Product has no live product-economics validation; and its external reconnaissance, which I used only as staff advice and never as SPIDER evidence - I did no browsing myself. CORRECTED: the brief proposes that Graph 'fix C-PARAM-INHERIT kernel integration'. That is wrong twice. Graph's allowed_code_roots are research/harness and research/graph, so Graph cannot touch src/ at all; and the defect is not an unwritten integration but an accepted, audited, unit-tested capability that is absent from the canonical tree, so the fix is a Product-scoped recovery pinned by hash, not a rewrite. The brief also offers Graph C-FRESHNESS as a fallback direction, which I reject because that next_gate requires a session/auth/drift substrate that does not exist here and would be a third consecutive MEASUREMENT_INVALID on transfer. REJECTED: the brief's physics reactivation proposal and its Frontier proposal both point at real Web assets - BrowserGym, WebChoreArena, CAP, live heterogeneous sites - that this runner cannot reach, and licensing two lanes to absent assets while two other lanes are already executing is the portfolio-level version of the local attractor. REJECTED SPECIFICALLY: the brief tells Frontier to execute the parent's epistemic decomposition. I read the exact frozen mandate text and it states that the inherited arm 'is never treated as a treatment arm' in that experiment, which means Frontier's own next experiment is barred by construction from producing the architecture verdict its charter exists to produce. A well-designed experiment that cannot decide anything is not worth a scarce lane, and I redirected Frontier to a question whose outcomes can. ADOPTED WITH REDIRECTION: the brief's single most decision-relevant external fact is that published systems (SCAFFOLD at +11.1 to +17.2 pts with cross-site transfer 35.9% vs 16.6%; WALT-style site-tool discovery at +20.5% over tool-free) occupy exactly the claim space SPIDER asserts. The brief offers this as context. I converted it into two concrete jobs - a pinned key-free reconstruction of the published competitors, assigned to the idle Intel lane, and a site-primitive substitution test, assigned to Frontier - because SPIDER's central comparison currently runs against cold discovery, literal replay and retrieval, which is close to a strawman field. Finally, the brief's questions_for_director asks whether SPIDER should reproduce external baselines. My answer is yes, but as pinned runnable reference arms inside SPIDER's own lane structure, not as an attempt to execute LLM-driven artifacts that require a key this runner does not have.
